title: Misleading Vividness
description: A small number of dramatic and vivid events are taken to outweigh a significant amount of statistical evidence.
logical_form:
Dramatic or vivid event X occurs (does not jibe with the majority of the statistical evidence).

Therefore, events of type X are likely to occur.

examples.example: In Detroit, there is a 10-year-old living on the street selling drugs to stay alive.  In Los Angeles, a 19-year-old prostitute works the streets.  America’s youth is certainly in serious trouble.
examples.explanation:
While the stories of the 10-year-old illegal pharmacist and the 19-year-old village bicycle are certainly disturbing, they are just two specific cases out of tens of millions -- a vast majority of youth live pretty regular lives, far from being considered in any “serious trouble”.  This is a form of *[appeal to emotion](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-Emotion)* that causes us to hold irrational beliefs about a population due to a few select cases.  The example could have featured two other youths:

In Detroit, there is a 10-year-old who plays the piano as beautifully as Beethoven.  In Los Angeles, a 19-year-old genius is getting her PhD in nuclear physics.  America’s youth is certainly something of which we can be proud.

examples.example: It was freezing today as it was yesterday.  My plants are now dead, and my birdbath turned to solid ice...and it is only October!  This global warming thing is a load of crap.
examples.explanation: Whether global warming is a “load of crap” or not, concluding that, by a couple of unusually cold days, is fallacious reasoning at its finest.

exceptions: If the cases featured are typical of the population in general, then no fallacy is committed.
tips: Don’t let your pessimism or optimism cloud your judgments on reality.
references: Nisbett, R. E., & Ross, L. (1980). *Human inference: strategies and shortcomings of social judgment*. Prentice-Hall.
description_et: Väike arv dramaatilisi ja elavaid sündmusi kaalub üles märkimisväärse hulga statistilisi tõendeid.
logical_form_et:
Toimub dramaatiline või elav sündmus X (ei ole vastuolus enamiku statistiliste tõenditega).

Seetõttu võivad X-tüüpi sündmused tekkida.
exceptions_et: Kui esiletoodud juhtumid on tüüpilised elanikkonnale üldiselt, siis ei tehta eksitusi.
tips_et: Ärge laske oma pessimismil või optimismil varjutada teie hinnanguid tegelikkuse kohta.

examples_et.example: Detroidis elab tänaval 10-aastane, kes müüb narkootikume, et elus püsida.  Los Angeleses töötab tänavatel 19-aastane prostituut.  Ameerika noored on kindlasti tõsistes raskustes.
examples_et.explanation:
Kuigi lood 10-aastasest illegaalsest apteekrist ja 19-aastasest külarattast on kahtlemata häirivad, on need vaid kaks konkreetset juhtumit kümnetest miljonitest – valdav enamus noori elab üsna tavalist elu, kaugel sellest, et neid “tõsistes hädades” käsitletaks.  See on *[emotsioonidele apelleerimine](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Appeal-to-Emotion)*, mis paneb meid mõne üksiku juhtumi tõttu valdama irratsionaalseid uskumusi elanikkonna kohta.  Näites oleks võinud olla kaks teist noort:

Detroidis on 10-aastane, kes mängib klaverit sama kaunilt kui Beethoven.  Los Angeleses omandab 19-aastane geenius doktorikraadi tuumafüüsikas.  Ameerika noored on kindlasti midagi, mille üle võime uhked olla.
